context.body: Solomon’s administrative achievement becomes the grievance that breaks the kingdom.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: Israel asks Rehoboam to lighten Solomon’s hard service; he rejects elder counsel, threatens heavier burdens, and the northern tribes revolt.
observations.label: Rehoboam rejects the plea for lighter service: action

observations.body: The people’s complaint names Solomon’s yoke as the inheritance under dispute.
observations.label: Rehoboam rejects the plea for lighter service: response

observations.body: your father made our yoke grievous · young men · heavier · Israel departed
observations.label: Words in 1 Kings 12:1–20

payload.posture: Read 1 Kings 12:1–20 as later memory and aftermath evidence before carrying it into another source.
payload.tension: The narrator relates the turn to the LORD’s word while preserving Rehoboam’s culpable choice.
payload.title: Rehoboam rejects the plea for lighter service
